# DG Delegated Full Review

Use this skill only when the user invokes it directly or an explicitly requested workflow invokes it. Do not select it automatically.

Use `$dg-engineering-writing-style` when available. Look for it in the repository's `./.agents/skills` folder.

Run the review outside the primary agent's context. Do not modify files, fix findings, or delegate from the review subagent.

## Workflow reference

May be selected by `$*-run-scoped-engineering-workflow` at step 6 through its review dispatcher. Standalone use remains supported. This skill owns the single review subagent; never route back through the personal dispatcher. Preserve any caller-supplied acceptance boundary alongside the review target.

## Resolve the target

- Preserve a pull request, branch, commit, diff, or other review target supplied by the user.
- Otherwise, review all staged, unstaged, and untracked changes in the current working directory.
- If the working tree is clean, review the current branch against its merge base with the configured upstream or default base branch.

## Run the review

Create exactly one read-only subagent or task in the current working directory. Use the host-specific path that matches the available tools without asking the user which host is running:

- In Codex, spawn a subagent (not a new user-visible task) and direct it to run `/review` for the resolved target.
- In Claude Code, use an `Agent` subagent and direct it to run `/review`, the alias for `/code-review`. Use `/code-review` if the alias is unavailable.
- In another agent host, use its task or subagent mechanism and give the worker the natural-language review instructions below.

If the worker cannot invoke the slash command, have that same worker follow these instructions instead. Do not start a replacement worker or perform the review in the primary context.

```text
Perform a read-only, defect-first review of the requested code changes. Inspect the complete diff and enough surrounding code and tests to verify each issue. Report only concrete, actionable regressions introduced by the change. List findings by severity with precise file and line references. If there are no qualifying findings, return "No findings." Do not modify files or delegate the review.
```

Wait for the worker to finish. Return its findings to the primary conversation, preserving priorities and file references. If the worker fails, report the failure instead of completing the review inline.

## Close the review task

Capture the result before cleanup.

- In Codex, close the completed subagent when a non-destructive close or archive action is available. Otherwise report that the runtime does not support cleanup.
- Claude Code subagents are ephemeral and need no separate archive action.
- In another host, close or archive the completed task when a non-destructive lifecycle action is available.

Do not permanently delete a transcript or worktree as a substitute for closing or archiving it.


ARGUMENTS: on the last commit

The review of `d387715c6` ("Mark failed/oversize assets") found one medium issue and two low ones. The reviewer didn't use `/code-review`, because that command starts its own helper agents, which this review had ruled out. It read the diff by hand, ran the three affected test files (86 tests pass), and confirmed each finding with a temporary test in the scratchpad, since deleted. No repo files were changed.

**1. Medium: a labelled embed loses its label when marked** (`apps/roam/src/utils/rewriteAssetLinks.ts:247-251`, `renderMarked`)
- **Problem:** `renderMarked` keeps the text after the pipe only when the asset kind is "file". PDF, audio and video embeds lose it.
- **Example:** `![[vault/a.pdf|the paper]]` with a failed upload becomes `[Failed to import](vault/a.pdf)`, and "the paper" is gone. `![[vault/a.mp3|the talk]]` behaves the same.
- **Cause:** The comment at line 286 says the pipe holds a width only on images. The check should drop the pipe text only for images, e.g. `kindOf(...) !== "image"`.
- **Why tests miss it:** They use a plain wikilink or a `.docx` embed, never a labelled PDF, audio or video embed.

**2. Low: marked links lose the author's percent-encoding** (`rewriteAssetLinks.ts:452`, `:220-225`, `linkDestination`)
- **Problem:** The marked link is built from the decoded locator, and `linkDestination` only re-encodes whitespace, parentheses and angle brackets.
- **Example:** `![](fig%231.png)` becomes `[Failed to import](fig#1.png)`, so `#1.png` reads as a URL fragment.
- **Example:** `![](vault/100%25.png)` becomes `…(vault/100%.png)`, which is an invalid escape.

**3. Low: a marked image inside a link produces broken markup** (`rewriteAssetLinks.ts:254`, `renderMarked`)
- **Problem:** A marked image is turned into a `[...]` link. The pattern explicitly supports an image inside a link (comment at lines 278-280), and before this commit a failed asset there was left as published.
- **Example:** `[![alt](vault/d.png)](https://x.org)` with a failed asset becomes `[[alt (Failed to import)](vault/d.png)](https://x.org)`. That starts with `[[`, which Roam reads as a page reference, and puts one link inside another, so neither link renders.

**Checked and fine:**
- Trailing punctuation on bare and angle-bracket URLs.
- A copied asset wins over a marked one when two spellings match.
- Oversize results are reused by hash.
- `FailedImport` no longer has the optional `sourceLocator`.

**Behavior change:** `importNodeAssets` now throws when it can't read the reference rows. Nothing in `apps/roam/src` calls it yet. Its docstring says the node "is retried by the next import", but that only holds if a future caller catches the error without moving the stored timestamp forward.

All three fixes work in the cases the reviewer reported. Two narrow cases of finding 3 still produce the wrong output. I reviewed this myself rather than through a reviewer agent: I read the diff, ran the tests and typecheck, and tried a few more inputs in a temporary test file, which I've deleted.

The 88 tests in `rewriteAssetLinks.test.ts` and `importNodeAssets.test.ts` pass, and `tsc` reports nothing in either file.

- **Fix 1, labels:** correct. `![[vault/a.png|2024]]` now reads "2024" as a size, but Obsidian reads it the same way, so that's fine.
- **Fix 2, percent-encoding:** correct.
  - `![](my%20file.png)` is kept as written.
  - `![](<my file.png>)` is encoded to `my%20file.png`.
- **Fix 4, docstring:** fine. Removing `sourcePath` and the `sourcePaths` map in `importNodeAssets` is clean.

**Fix 3 still misses two cases.** The check only looks at the one character before `![`:

- **Image not at the start of the link label:** it still nests one link inside another.
  - Input: `[see ![alt](vault/d.png)](https://x.org)`
  - Output: `[see [alt (Failed to import)](vault/d.png)](https://x.org)`
- **A plain `[` before the image:** a bracket that doesn't open a link still counts, so the image loses its destination.
  - Input: `[![alt](vault/d.png) plain bracket`
  - Output: `[alt (Failed to import) plain bracket`

Both are rare. The first is still broken, just less often than before. Checking that the image sits inside a real link label would catch both, but the change probably isn't worth it unless Obsidian notes actually contain this pattern.

**One fragile spot:** `args.at(-2)` finds the match position only because `LINK_PATTERN` has no named groups. If someone adds one, `replace` passes an extra argument, and the image-in-link check reads the wrong value without any error. Using `args.find((arg) => typeof arg === "number")` would still work after that change.

I fixed both cases the review agent found. All 409 tests pass, tsc and eslint are clean, and nothing is committed.

- Image in the middle of a link label: the old check only looked at the single character before ![. It now checks that the image really sits inside a link label on its line: there's an unclosed [ before it and ]( after it, with no other brackets or line breaks in between. [see ![alt](vault/d.png) here](https://x.org) now becomes [see alt (Failed to import) here](https://x.org).
- A [ that doesn't open a link: [![alt](vault/d.png) plain bracket now keeps its link, giving [[alt (Failed to import)](vault/d.png) plain bracket. The stray [ is the author's, and with no ]] after it Roam shouldn't read it as a page reference.
- Finding the match position: it now uses args.find((arg) => typeof arg === "number"), so adding a named group to LINK_PATTERN won't silently break the check.

I added a test for each of the two cases. The check for a real link label is the new isInsideLinkLabel helper in rewriteAssetLinks.ts.

The two cases from the last round are fixed. One realistic case still breaks: two images in the same link label. I checked your change myself: I read `isInsideLinkLabel`, tried more inputs in a temporary test file (deleted), and ran the full Roam test suite. All 423 tests pass. You reported 409, so the count may differ because of what each of us ran; either way nothing fails.

**Still broken:** two images in one link label, like a row of badges.
- Input: `[see ![a](vault/d.png) and ![b](vault/d.png)](https://x.org)`
- Output: `[see [a (Failed to import)](vault/d.png) and [b (Failed to import)](vault/d.png)](https://x.org)`
- Cause: the check requires no `[` or `]` between the image and the closing `](`. For the first image, the second image's `![b](` is in that stretch, so the check fails and both images become nested links.
- The same thing happens with no space between the images: `[![a](…)![b](…)](https://x.org)`.
- Possible fix: skip over whole `![…](…)` images when scanning to the closing `](`. Or, more simply, allow `![...](...)` in the text that comes after the image.

**Minor, probably not worth fixing:**
- A label that already contains brackets, such as `[see [x] ![alt](vault/d.png)](https://x.org)`, is still nested. That's rare in practice.
- `[![alt](vault/d.png)]]` becomes `[[alt (Failed to import)](vault/d.png)]]`, which Roam could read as a page reference. The input is contrived.

**Correct:**
- An image in the middle of a label: `[see ![alt](vault/d.png) here](https://x.org)` becomes `[see alt (Failed to import) here](https://x.org)`.
- A stray `[` before an image keeps the image as a link.
- Inline code in the label doesn't confuse the check.
- The match position now comes from `args.find(...)`, so adding a named group to `LINK_PATTERN` won't break it.
The first case should be repaired.

The two-images case is already fixed in the working tree, so I didn't edit anything. The current `rewriteAssetLinks.ts` has the change and a test for it; the coding agent presumably added both after its last report.

- **The fix:** a new `LABEL_TEXT` pattern treats each whole image as ordinary label text. The before and after checks both use it and stay within the image's own line.
- **The new test:** "marks every image in one link label, as in a row of badges" covers the input from last round and the version with no space between the images:
  - `[see ![a](vault/d.png) and ![b](vault/d.png)](https://x.org)` becomes `[see a (Failed to import) and b (Failed to import)](https://x.org)`.
  - `[![a](vault/d.png)![b](vault/d.png)](https://x.org)` becomes `[a (Failed to import)b (Failed to import)](https://x.org)`.
- **Tests:** all 73 tests in `rewriteAssetLinks.test.ts` pass.
- **Slow-matching risk:** low. The two ways the pattern can match text can't overlap, and each check only scans the image's own line.

Nothing is committed.
